solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sweet sort of complexion

definitions.meaning: a dessert of fruit served with cream, the summer dish
a fair, rosy, flawless skin is described with this phrase

explanation.surface: A puzzling pairing: something sugary and a kind of skin tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a pudding of soft fruit with cream; figuratively a pink-and-white, smooth skin tone.

clue.text: Show-jumpers take lead from Princess Royal before making a self-adjustment

indicators.note: lead from takes the first letter of Princess

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for royalty
making means forming

indicators.note: adjustment means the letters are altered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Equestrian show-jumping: Princess Anne, the Princess Royal, adjusts her position before a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: Pun: circus insects that jump as part of a performance are literally show-jumpers.

clue.text: Drives a touring coach

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A driver takes a coach on tour.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a coach gives guidance, as a counsellor or mentor does.

clue.text: Greeting from ship's crew to fish

parts.note: a ship's hands are its crew
hake is a fish

explanation.surface: Sailors call out a greeting to a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: clasping palms is a common salutation when meeting someone.

clue.text: Rump of small bird

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Pointing to the hindquarters of a little bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the rear part or back end of something, as of a ship.

clue.text: Go into new topless pub like the Red Fox?

indicators.note: into places one piece inside the other
topless removes the first letter

parts.note: a local is one's neighbourhood pub
a go is a turn

explanation.surface: An invitation to try a new topless bar called the Red Fox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' leaves OCAL and 'into' sets the go inside. 'The Red Fox' reads as a pub name but is the animal; a 'local' is British for one's regular neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: foxes are mainly active at night, hence the question mark.

clue.text: In Roman times, one who conspired to report wrongdoer

definitions.text: In Roman times, one who conspired

indicators.note: to report means to say aloud, so the clue word's sound is used

parts.note: a wrongdoer is a sinner

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman plotter informs on a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Lucius Cornelius Cinna was among the plotters who assassinated Julius Caesar.

clue.text: Livid gardener sacked after finishing early

indicators.note: sacked means ransacked and disordered, so the letters are rearranged
finishing early means the word stops short, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A gardener is furious at being fired after knocking off early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing early' trims GARDENER to GARDENE; 'sacked' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone livid is furious, extremely angry.

clue.text: Address for solicitor nearly lost in sea to north of China

indicators.note: in a down clue, to the north of means placed above, so earlier
in places the rearranged letters within the sea

parts.note: Med is the Mediterranean Sea

indicators.note: lost means astray, so the letters go astray and are rearranged

parts.note: china means mate, from cockney rhyming slang china plate

explanation.surface: A lawyer almost lost at sea north of China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' scrambles the adverb to YLEARN, which 'in' places within the Mediterranean. China is cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: courtroom lawyers politely refer to opposing counsel this way.

clue.text: Fresh green veg chopped into cold dish, ideally

indicators.note: fresh here means made anew, so the letters are rearranged
chopped says the word veg has its tail cut off, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A cook chops greens to toss into a cold dish, as a recipe would ideally have it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped' trims VEG to VE; 'Fresh' rearranges GREEN plus VE (GREENVE) into the answer. The definition alludes to the saying that this dish is best served cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverb: retaliation is a dish best served cold, so cold dish describes payback ideally delivered after waiting.

clue.text: Key element of decent rallies

indicators.note: element of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tennis commentator notes that decent rallies are a key part of the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something key is pivotal, at the heart of matters, i.e. principal.

clue.text: Blood group like one son's group

parts.note: O is one of the human blood groups
as means like, in comparisons
I is the Roman numeral for one
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A comparison of blood types: one person's group matches their son's.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the final word: the 1990s Manchester rock band, not a blood group.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Gallagher brothers' Britpop band from Manchester is a famous musical group.

clue.text: Suffering nerves in northern Europe, ruler having left country

indicators.note: having left says the ruler's letters depart from the country's name

parts.note: Algeria is a country in North Africa
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword's usual ruler

explanation.surface: Someone in northern Europe is in pain now that their monarch has fled the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having left' strips the Queen from the North African country, leaving ALGIA; 'Suffering nerves' is a noun phrase for nerve pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical term for intense pain felt along a nerve, so the suffering lies in the nerves themselves.

clue.text: Greed possibly shown as roast lamb starter demolished in 30 seconds?

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the half-minute

parts.note: half a minute, so the word minute cut in half

indicators.note: demolished means wrecked and rebuilt, so the letters are rearranged
starter takes the first letter of lamb

explanation.surface: A greedy diner wolfs down a roast lamb starter in half a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: Thirty seconds is half a minute, so half that word's letters; 'demolished' scrambles the meat plus its starter into ORTALS, which 'in' puts inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: avarice is one of the seven deadly vices in Christian teaching, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Where clip is undone, with bust revealed initially?

definitions.text: Where clip is undone, with bust revealed initially?

indicators.note: undone means unfastened and disarranged, so the letters are rearranged
initially takes the first letter of revealed

explanation.surface: A venue where clasps are unfastened and chests exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: CLIP, BUST and R (from 'revealed') are mixed by 'undone'; the whole clue also describes the place.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an adult venue where performers undress, unfastening clothing and exposing themselves.

clue.text: Artist fellow is a gas

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword's usual artist
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A chatty painter is described as a real gas, a laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a radioactive noble element that is a gas at room temperature.

clue.text: People on heroin? You can bet on it

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above

parts.note: a race is a people
horse is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Talk of people on drugs and of gambling.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: punters wager on a thoroughbred running at the track.

clue.text: Fool about making some gunpowder

parts.note: a nit is a fool, a nitwit
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: An idiot fooling around with explosives.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is one ingredient of black powder, hence only part of it.

clue.text: Go in to riot, to see what one can get away with

definitions.text: to see what one can get away with

parts.note: a go is a try

indicators.note: riot means run wild, so the letters run wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Joining a riot just to test how far one can push it.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: chancing one's arm, testing boundaries to discover what is tolerated.

clue.text: Moved house while having to declare otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Someone moved home and had to tell the authorities something different.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who moved house has shifted to a new home, i.e. changed address.

clue.text: Pudding recipe leaving apricot out? Ace!

indicators.note: out means out of order, so the letters are rearranged
leaving says those letters depart from the fruit's name

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin
A is the abbreviation for ace, as on playing cards

explanation.surface: A pudding recipe that leaves out apricots, met with delight.
explanation.walkthrough: APRICOT without R gives APICOT, rearranged by 'out', then A.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sweet milky dish made with cassava pearls, a British school dessert.

clue.text: Item used when cooking fish at home? Doctor has one

parts.note: fry are young fish
in means at home
GP, general practitioner, is a family doctor
an means one, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Asking what you'd use to cook fish at home, then noting the doctor owns one.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a shallow, long-handled skillet is kitchen equipment used for cooking food in fat.

clue.text: Sauce bottle

definitions.meaning: bottle is British slang for courage

explanation.surface: A condiment and its container.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean boldness: cheek, and British slang for courage.

clue.text: Famous Indian female only up on sport

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above
up in a down clue means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a hen party is female only, so hen means female only
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A well-known Indian woman who cares only about sport.
explanation.walkthrough: HEN read upwards gives NEH, then RU, rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Jawaharlal, India's first prime minister, is a celebrated Indian.

clue.text: Over-excited and somewhat pushy person

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Describing an overbearing, keyed-up individual.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: someone wound up and highly strung, unable to calm down.

clue.text: Penetrate even bits of wall in the gut

parts.note: to penetrate is to enter

indicators.note: even bits of takes the second and fourth letters of wall

explanation.surface: Something breaching the lining of the intestine.
explanation.definitionFit: Medical adjective meaning involving or via the intestine, as in feeding by tube to the stomach.

clue.text: Heard working girl lament one cause of sexual arousal

indicators.note: heard says the words are spoken, giving the sound of the entry

parts.note: a working girl is a prostitute, a whore; lament means moan

explanation.surface: A prostitute overheard bemoaning what drives her clients' desires.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'whore moan' gives the entry; 'working girl' is a euphemism for a sex worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: testosterone and oestrogen are body chemicals that drive libido.

clue.text: Worried as volunteers dub film

indicators.note: worried means disturbed and shaken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Anxious because unpaid helpers are dubbing a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Billy Wilder's 1950 Hollywood classic starring Gloria Swanson.
